intro:
HSR to West Kowloon; chartered van all day for photo stops, one area at a time
East Kowloon: Choi Hung Estate; through the tunnel to Quarry Bay: Monster Building
Wan Chai: lunch at Kam's roast goose, Capital Café; Ding Ding tram west to Central
Central: escalator, Tai Cheong, Lan Fong Yuen; van up to the Peak, Sky Terrace 428, Lugard Road, Peak Tram down
Star Ferry to Tsim Sha Tsui: Mammy Pancake, Ocean Terminal Deck, 1881 Heritage, Clock Tower, Avenue of Stars
Optional: dinner at Tim Ho Wan in West Kowloon Station before clearance

items.title: K Hotel → Guangzhou South Station (广州南站)
Enter station, security check
items.note: Trains to Hong Kong require earlier arrival; 40 min should be allowed.
items.tip: Documents for entering Hong Kong and returning to the mainland must be carried; check once more before leaving.

items.title: HSR: Guangzhou South → Hong Kong West Kowloon (香港西九龙)
items.tip: HSR tickets should be bought as soon as sales open; year-end tickets sell out fast.

items.title: West Kowloon Station border clearance
items.note: Mainland exit and Hong Kong entry are both done inside the station.

items.title: Hong Kong route (chartered van)

route.section: East Kowloon and Quarry Bay: photo stops
route.title: West Kowloon Station → Choi Hung Estate (彩虹邨)
route.desc: Van, ~25 min
route.pick: West Kowloon Station car park, level B2, pick-up/drop-off point (15 min free for pick-up); confirmed with the driver by WhatsApp after clearance
route.drop: Choi Hung Estate car park (the basketball court is on its roof); whether the van can enter is to be confirmed with the driver

route.title: Choi Hung Estate (彩虹邨)
route.walk: Stairs from the car-park entrance up to the roof
route.desc: Rainbow-painted blocks of an older public estate; the basketball court on the car-park roof is the best-known photo spot. ~3 min up the stairs and ~10 min of photos, ~15 min in all; the driver waits at the drop-off.
route.tip: This is a residential estate: photos should be taken quietly without blocking residents, and any no-photography notice on site should be followed.

route.title: Choi Hung → Quarry Bay (鲗鱼涌)
route.desc: Van, ~20 min via the Eastern Harbour Crossing, which comes out at Quarry Bay
route.pick: Where the group was dropped at Choi Hung (the driver waits)
route.drop: Outside Lincoln House, Taikoo Place (太古坊林肯大厦), King's Road, a stop once used by a hotel shuttle; whether the van can stop is to be confirmed with the driver

route.title: Monster Building (怪兽大厦)
route.walk: A few minutes across King's Road, into the courtyard from Yick Cheong Building
route.desc: Five linked old residential blocks; from the courtyard the windows tower on every side. A filming location for Transformers: Age of Extinction. A few photos, ~10 min there and back; the driver waits at the drop-off.
route.tip: This is a residential estate: photos should be taken quietly without blocking residents, and any no-photography notice on site should be followed.

route.title: Quarry Bay → Wan Chai
route.desc: Van, ~15 min
route.pick: Outside Lincoln House, Taikoo Place (the driver waits)
route.drop: A side street near Kam's Roast Goose (226 Hennessy Road); Hennessy Road has tram tracks and bus stops, so the spot is chosen by the driver

route.section: Wan Chai: roast goose lunch, café
route.title: Kam's Roast Goose (甘牌烧鹅)
route.walk: From the drop-off to 226 Hennessy Road
route.desc: Michelin-starred roast goose; the goose leg is the order. Doors open at 11:30; arriving ~11:25 and queuing before opening should get a first-sitting table. Queue plus lunch: ~50 min.
route.tip: No bookings; a queue number is taken on arrival. One visitor reported 20–30 min even off-peak. The busiest time is after 12:30.

food.name: Roast goose leg rice (烧鹅腿饭)
food.desc: Roast goose rice can be upgraded to the leg for a supplement

route.title: Capital Café (華星冰室)
route.desc: A well-known cha chaan teng: right after lunch a takeaway yuenyeung or milk tea is enough, with a pineapple bun if anyone is hungry. ~15 min.

food.name: Yuenyeung, milk tea (鸳鸯、奶茶)
food.desc: Coffee mixed with milk tea, Hong Kong's signature drink

food.name: Scrambled-egg toast, pineapple bun (炒蛋多士、菠萝油)

route.section: Tram to Central: escalator, egg tarts, milk tea
route.title: Ding Ding tram (叮叮车)
route.walk: Back to Hennessy Road for a westbound tram (towards Central / Kennedy Town)
route.desc: Century-old tram; front seats on the upper deck give the best street view. ~25 min to Central; a Wise card or Apple Pay is tapped when getting off. The van goes ahead and waits at Tai Cheong Bakery at 14:00.

route.title: Central–Mid-Levels Escalator (中环至半山自动扶梯)
route.walk: Off the tram in Central; ~5 min on foot to the escalator start on Queen's Road Central
route.desc: Billed as the world's longest covered outdoor escalator system; free. It runs uphill in the afternoon; two or three sections reach Lyndhurst Terrace, ~15 min including the walk.

route.title: Tai Cheong Bakery (泰昌饼家)
route.walk: At the Lyndhurst Terrace exit of the escalator
route.desc: Flaky egg tarts as an afternoon snack, eaten on the go, then takeaway milk tea at Lan Fong Yuen; ~25 min. The stone steps of Pottinger Street (砵典乍街) are right at the corner, good for a quick photo. Back at Tai Cheong's door for the 14:00 pick-up.
route.tip: Pottinger Street is a stepped granite lane lined with stalls; the stones are uneven, so footing should be watched.

food.name: Lan Fong Yuen (兰芳园)
food.desc: 2 Gage St, ~1 min away; the original silk-stocking milk tea, taken away

food.name: LINLEE, Lyndhurst Terrace (LINLEE中环摆花街店)

route.section: The Peak: Sky Terrace, Lugard Road, tram down
route.title: Central → The Peak
route.desc: Van up, ~20 min; the uphill tram queue is avoided.
route.pick: Outside Tai Cheong Bakery, 35 Lyndhurst Terrace: the Travel Industry Council's holiday traffic notes allow coaches to pick up and drop off on Lyndhurst Terrace, but vehicles must leave at once and may not wait; the van is called by WhatsApp once everyone is ready. If the driver says no, his chosen spot is used
route.drop: The Peak Galleria (山顶广场) car park, next to the Peak Tower (the Peak Tower has no car park)

route.title: Madame Tussauds Hong Kong (杜莎夫人蜡像馆)
route.desc: Close-up photos with wax figures of stars and athletes; ~45 min. The times below assume it is skipped; if visited, Lugard Road is dropped to keep the 15:30 pick-up.

route.title: Sky Terrace 428 (凌霄阁摩天台428)
route.walk: From the Peak Galleria to the Peak Tower, then by escalator to the top
route.desc: A 360° deck 428 m above sea level over Victoria Harbour and Hong Kong Island; the classic skyline photo without a hill walk. ~25 min.
route.tip: The Peak is windier and colder than the city; a jacket should be brought. Tickets should be bought online in advance: a round-trip Peak Tram + Sky Terrace 428 combo covers the ride down; a one-way ticket may be valid uphill only, which should be checked when booking.

food.name: Pacific Coffee, Peak Tower (Pacific Coffee凌霄阁)
food.desc: Local Hong Kong coffee chain; a short break for the adults

route.title: Lugard Road lookout (卢吉道观景台)
route.walk: ~10 min along flat, shaded Lugard Road from the Peak Tower
route.desc: A free lookout over Victoria Harbour and the Central towers; ~25 min there and back, back at the Peak Tower by 15:10.

route.title: Peak Tram down (山顶缆车下山)
route.walk: The Peak Tram station inside the Peak Tower
route.desc: Century-old funicular; the slope is so steep that the towers outside seem to lean, which kids remember. ~7 min down to the Central Terminus on Garden Road.
route.tip: The afternoon queue down is usually shorter than the queue up; one traveller reported ~20 min, but it can be long before evening. A ticket reseller says a queue number is now taken by scanning the "Queue Easy" QR code at the Peak station; on-site rules apply. If a long wait is shown, the driver is messaged to pick up at the Peak Galleria instead and go straight to the Star Ferry.

route.title: Peak Tram Central Terminus → Central Star Ferry Pier (中环天星码头)
route.desc: Van, ~10 min
route.pick: Near the Peak Tram Central Terminus, Garden Road; Garden Road is busy, so the spot is chosen by the driver (whether the driveway of The Murray hotel next door can be used is worth asking)
route.drop: The loading area outside Central Pier 7 (a Transport Department document lists it as drop-off only)

route.section: Tsim Sha Tsui: egg waffles, harbour photos, 1881 Heritage
route.title: Star Ferry: Central → Tsim Sha Tsui (天星小轮)
route.desc: Century-old ferry; ~20 min for tickets, the wait and the crossing, with the skyline on both sides. Tickets are bought by card at the pier's self-service machines.

route.title: Mammy Pancake (媽咪雞蛋仔)
route.walk: At the Tsim Sha Tsui Star Ferry Pier, off the boat
route.desc: Egg waffles listed in the Michelin street food guide, crisp outside and soft inside; an afternoon snack on the go.

food.name: Egg waffle (鸡蛋仔)
food.desc: Original is the classic; chocolate and other flavours too

route.tip: Small stalls like this may take only cash or Octopus; card or Apple Pay should be checked first, and the stop skipped if neither works.

route.title: Ocean Terminal Deck (海运大厦观景台)
route.walk: ~8 min, indoors through Harbour City to the end of Ocean Terminal
route.desc: A free harbourside rooftop facing Victoria Harbour and Hong Kong Island; ~15 min. Afterwards the route heads east without doubling back.

route.title: 1881 Heritage (前水警总部)
route.walk: ~10 min through Harbour City and along Canton Road to Salisbury Road
route.desc: The former Marine Police Headquarters; its colonial lawns and arcades photograph well, and a free Christmas installation is usually up at year end. ~20 min.
route.tip: This year's Christmas installation has not been announced; what is on show should be checked on the day.

route.title: Tsim Sha Tsui Clock Tower (尖沙咀钟楼)
route.walk: ~5 min across Salisbury Road, beside the Star Ferry pier
route.desc: The century-old clock tower left from the former Kowloon–Canton Railway terminus; a quick harbourside photo.

route.title: Avenue of Stars (星光大道)
route.walk: East along the waterfront from the Clock Tower
route.desc: The harbourfront promenade with the Bruce Lee statue, facing the island skyline; ~20 min of walking and photos to the K11 MUSEA pick-up. Close to sunset, the light is at its best.

route.title: Tsim Sha Tsui → West Kowloon Station
route.desc: Van, ~20–25 min; evening traffic is expected.
route.pick: K11 MUSEA private-car pick-up/drop-off area, level B2 (the mall beside the Avenue of Stars); if it cannot be used, the pick-up points on Salisbury Road (westbound), to be confirmed with the driver
route.drop: West Kowloon Station car park, level B2, pick-up/drop-off point

items.note: The van is hired 10:00–18:00 and the driver is contacted by WhatsApp; every pick-up and drop-off point is marked below. All pick-ups are on the hour or half hour; on the walking stretches the van goes ahead to the next pick-up point.
items.tip:
For the driver (WhatsApp): Dec 30 van hire, 2 adults plus kids.
10:00 pick-up at West Kowloon Station car park B2 pick-up/drop-off point → Choi Hung Estate car park
~10:40 pick-up at Choi Hung Estate car park (please wait ~15 min while we take photos) → outside Lincoln House, Taikoo Place, Quarry Bay
~11:10 pick-up outside Lincoln House (please wait ~10 min while we take photos) → near Kam's Roast Goose, 226 Hennessy Road, Wan Chai (we then take the tram to Central)
14:00 pick-up outside Tai Cheong Bakery, 35 Lyndhurst Terrace → Peak Galleria car park
15:30 pick-up at the Peak Tram Central Terminus, Garden Road → Central Pier 7
17:30 pick-up at K11 MUSEA B2 pick-up/drop-off area, Tsim Sha Tsui → ~18:00 drop-off at West Kowloon Station car park B2
If a pick-up point is not allowed, please use the nearest legal spot and tell us by WhatsApp.
Vans are usually hired by the hour; hours, harbour-tunnel tolls and parking (if the van parks at Choi Hung or the Peak Galleria) should be agreed first. Many Central streets are no-stopping zones, so the van is called once everyone is ready.

items.title: Dinner: Tim Ho Wan, West Kowloon Station (添好运西九龙站)
items.note: On level B1M of West Kowloon Station, before clearance. If taken, clearance and the train move ~50 min later, with the hotel reached ~21:10.
items.tip: All are on level B1M, before clearance. Payment should be checked in store (review sites list Visa, Mastercard and Apple Pay for Tim Ho Wan; the others are unconfirmed). The shop list comes from older sources and may have changed.

food.name: Tim Ho Wan, West Kowloon Station (添好运西九龙站)
food.desc: Dim sum chain recognised by Michelin

food.name: Baked BBQ pork buns (酥皮焗叉烧包)
Shrimp siu mai, har gow (鲜虾烧卖、虾饺)
Pig liver rice roll (黄沙猪润肠)
food.desc: Strong flavour; for the adults to try

food.name: Mao Mao Eat by Tsui Wah (翠华西九龙站)
food.desc: Backup: Hong Kong-style café with milk tea, pineapple buns, cart noodles and rice plates; used if the Tim Ho Wan queue is too long

food.name: Ramen Bari-Uma (西九龙站)
food.desc: Backup: Japanese ramen, an easy choice for kids

food.name: Maxim's Cakes (美心西饼西九龙站)
food.desc: Backup: cakes and bread to eat on the train if time is short

items.title: HSR: West Kowloon → Guangzhou South
items.note: ~50 min; times follow the ticket booked.

items.title: Dinner: near the hotel
items.tip: Skipped if dinner was taken at West Kowloon Station; otherwise dinner is late and a snack on the train helps.

notice: No Octopus card or coins needed. Ding Ding tram: a Wise card or Apple Pay is tapped when getting off; adult HK$3.3, child HK$1.6. Star Ferry: tickets are bought by card or QR at the pier's self-service machines; weekday adult HK$5.0, child HK$2.9. Both rides total HK$8.3 per adult and HK$4.5 per child. Foreign cards may incur cross-border fees.
